$comment: Lane definitions: the ten jobs a fleet can hand out, one per free model. No model names live here - a lane says what it is for, and a profile says which model serves it. The compiler reads this file to write agent.<lane> into the generated config, and `install` links prompts/ so the prompt body is live-editable.

build.description: Writes and verifies code. Use when the plan is settled and files need to change.

plan.description: Turns a request into an executable plan. Use when a task is vague, spans several files, or two people could disagree about what done means.

reviewer.description: Reviews a change in two passes and never edits. Use after a build step, before a commit or a release decision.

locate.description: Finds where something lives and reports file:line evidence. Use before planning or changing anything, to close a gap in what is already known.

verify.description: Runs the project's checks and reports the real result. Use before claiming a task is done.

vision.description: Reads an image, a screenshot or a diagram and reports what is in it. Use when the answer depends on pixels and not on a text file.

doc.description: Reads a long document or a spec and reports what it says. Use for a paper, a manual, or a specification the code has to match.

schema.description: Produces a JSON object or a JSON schema that matches one. Use when the output has to be parsed by a program and not read by a person.

sweep.description: Scans a lot of code mechanically and reports the matches. Use for bulk sweeps where speed matters more than judgement.

longform.description: Reads a very long document set, or writes several different versions of one answer. Use for a megabyte of context, or when the task wants alternatives rather than one answer.
